translations.answer: Gravity-View coordinates can reduce pitch- and roll-related world-motion drift in monocular human recovery, but the resulting SMPL-X trajectory remains an upstream candidate and must pass robot retargeting, collision, support, and dynamics checks before use as a WBC reference.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Camera-relative rotation and human detections are available.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Robot feasibility is evaluated by a separate retargeting and dynamics gate.
translations.applicability.robots.0: SMPL-X upstream data; target robot unspecified.
translations.confidence_rationale: Two world-motion benchmarks and the pinned official implementation support reduced orientation and trajectory drift; confidence is capped because robot feasibility is not evaluated.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines Gravity-View recovery and reports world-motion improvements and remaining drift.
translations.evidence.0.title: World-Grounded Human Motion Recovery via Gravity-View Coordinates
translations.title: Can world-grounded human motion recovered from a moving-camera video be used directly as a robot reference?
